description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Ultrasonic Distance Meter (UDM)

questions.question: What is the governing formula used to calculate one-way target distance in pulse-echo ultrasonic measurement?
questions.explanation: Because the acoustic pulse travels to the target reflector and returns back, the wave traverses twice the distance (2d = v * t, hence d = v * t / 2).

questions.question: Why is the elapsed round-trip time-of-flight (t) divided by 2 in distance calculation?
options: The sound wave traverses the distance twice: to the target and back as an echo
Because only half of the piezoelectric crystal is active during receive mode
To compensate for the 50% duty cycle of the 40 kHz square wave trigger
Because sound velocity doubles upon acoustic reflection at the barrier
questions.answer: The sound wave traverses the distance twice: to the target and back as an echo
questions.correct_option: The sound wave traverses the distance twice: to the target and back as an echo
questions.explanation: Pulse-echo kinematics measures total round-trip trajectory 2d. Dividing by two yields the true one-way standoff distance.

questions.question: How does ambient air temperature (T) affect the speed of sound and uncalibrated distance measurements?
options: Sound travels faster at higher temperatures; uncalibrated sensors underestimate target distance
Sound travels slower at higher temperatures; uncalibrated sensors underestimate target distance
Temperature has no effect on longitudinal acoustic speed in diatomic air
Sound travels faster at higher temperatures; uncalibrated sensors overestimate target distance
questions.answer: Sound travels faster at higher temperatures; uncalibrated sensors underestimate target distance
questions.correct_option: Sound travels faster at higher temperatures; uncalibrated sensors underestimate target distance
questions.explanation: Acoustic velocity increases with temperature (v ≈ 331.3 + 0.606 * T). If sound travels faster, the echo returns sooner, causing an uncalibrated timer to report a shorter distance.

questions.question: What physical mechanism creates the blind zone / dead zone (~2 to 4 cm) in ultrasonic transducers?
options: Mechanical crystal ringing immediately after pulse excitation obscures returning close-in echoes
Complete acoustic phase cancellation by destructive atmospheric interference
Electronic saturation of the comparator by background electromagnetic radiation
Total absorption of 40 kHz acoustic energy by air moisture within 4 cm
questions.answer: Mechanical crystal ringing immediately after pulse excitation obscures returning close-in echoes
questions.correct_option: Mechanical crystal ringing immediately after pulse excitation obscures returning close-in echoes
questions.explanation: The piezoelectric ceramic element continues to mechanically resonate and ring after firing; echoes returning during this decay window cannot be differentiated by the receiver comparator.

questions.question: In the linear calibration model d_meas = a * d_ref + b, what do parameters a and b represent?
options: a is the sensitivity slope (gain factor, ideal = 1.0) and b is the zero-distance offset intercept
a is acoustic attenuation in dB/m and b is receiver threshold voltage in volts
a is ambient atmospheric pressure and b is temperature in Celsius
a is piezoelectric resonant frequency and b is acoustic wavelength in air
questions.answer: a is the sensitivity slope (gain factor, ideal = 1.0) and b is the zero-distance offset intercept
questions.correct_option: a is the sensitivity slope (gain factor, ideal = 1.0) and b is the zero-distance offset intercept
questions.explanation: Linear regression calibration models the sensor response where a represents scaling sensitivity (ideally 1.0000) and b accounts for hardware latch latencies and acoustic center setback.

questions.question: Why is 40 kHz commonly selected as the operating acoustic center frequency for ultrasonic distance transceivers?
options: It is safely above the human audible limit (20 kHz) with low atmospheric absorption and compact piezoelectric element size
40 kHz is the electromagnetic resonant frequency of air molecules
Lower frequencies cannot reflect off metallic or acrylic barriers
Higher frequencies travel faster than the standard speed of sound
questions.answer: It is safely above the human audible limit (20 kHz) with low atmospheric absorption and compact piezoelectric element size
questions.correct_option: It is safely above the human audible limit (20 kHz) with low atmospheric absorption and compact piezoelectric element size
questions.explanation: 40 kHz is inaudible to human hearing, suffers manageable attenuation in ambient air compared to megahertz ultrasound, and matches the natural mechanical resonance of small ceramic discs.

questions.question: What causes acoustic specular reflection failure when the target barrier is tilted away from perpendicular alignment?
options: The reflected acoustic wavepacket deflects away from the receiver transducer according to the law of reflection
The frequency of ultrasound shifts above 100 kHz due to Doppler compression
The sound wave penetrates through the barrier without reflecting
questions.answer: The reflected acoustic wavepacket deflects away from the receiver transducer according to the law of reflection
questions.correct_option: The reflected acoustic wavepacket deflects away from the receiver transducer according to the law of reflection
questions.explanation: Smooth surfaces act as specular reflectors. If the incident acoustic beam is tilted away from normal incidence (perpendicularity), reflected energy bounces away from the receiver port.

questions.question: What is the speed of sound in dry air at standard room temperature (T = 20.0 °C)?
What is the role of the 10 µs trigger pulse applied to the ultrasonic module (such as HC-SR04)?
options: It commands the internal microcontroller to burst an 8-cycle 40 kHz ultrasonic wavepacket
It powers the piezoelectric transducer directly for the entire measurement duration
It discharges static electricity from the acoustic bench guide rails
It calibrates the analog-to-digital converter clock to absolute zero
questions.answer: It commands the internal microcontroller to burst an 8-cycle 40 kHz ultrasonic wavepacket
questions.correct_option: It commands the internal microcontroller to burst an 8-cycle 40 kHz ultrasonic wavepacket
questions.explanation: A 10 µs high-level TTL pulse at the trigger pin initiates the module's burst sequence (8 cycles of 40 kHz) and primes the echo receiver latch.

questions.question: Given a measured distance d_meas and calibrated parameters a (slope) and b (offset), how is the corrected distance d_cal computed?
questions.answer: d_cal = (d_meas - b) / a
questions.correct_option: d_cal = (d_meas - b) / a
questions.explanation: Inverting the linear calibration equation d_meas = a * d_ref + b yields the corrected true standoff distance d_cal = (d_meas - b) / a.

questions.question: Why is ultrasound typically defined as acoustic waves with frequencies above 20 kHz?
options: 20 kHz is the upper threshold of normal human hearing
Acoustic attenuation in air drops to zero above 20 kHz
Air molecules cannot vibrate below 20 kHz
questions.answer: 20 kHz is the upper threshold of normal human hearing
questions.correct_option: 20 kHz is the upper threshold of normal human hearing
questions.explanation: In acoustics, ultrasound comprises mechanical longitudinal vibrations above the human audible limit (~20 Hz to 20,000 Hz).

questions.question: What is the common operating resonant frequency of standard ultrasonic distance modules such as HC-SR04?
questions.answer: 40 kHz
questions.correct_option: 40 kHz
questions.explanation: 40 kHz is the industry standard for airborne rangefinding, providing an optimal compromise between atmospheric attenuation and directional resolution.

questions.question: At 40 kHz, what is the acoustic wavelength λ in room-temperature air (v = 343 m/s)?
How does ambient air temperature T (in Celsius) affect the speed of sound v in air?
options: v is completely independent of temperature
questions.explanation: Sound speed in an ideal gas scales as √(T_kelvin). The linear Taylor expansion around 0°C is v ≈ 331.3 + 0.606 * T (°C).

questions.question: If an uncalibrated ultrasonic sensor assumes v = 340 m/s on a cold day where actual v = 328 m/s, how will the calculated distance compare to true distance?
options: The calculated distance will be larger than the true distance
The calculated distance will be smaller than the true distance
The calculated distance will be exact
The sensor will fail to detect echoes
questions.answer: The calculated distance will be larger than the true distance
questions.correct_option: The calculated distance will be larger than the true distance
questions.explanation: Distance d = v_assumed * t / 2. Since v_assumed (340) > v_actual (328), the calculated distance overestimates true distance by ~3.7%.

questions.question: What is the primary physical reason for the 'blind zone' (minimum measuring distance ~2 cm to 3 cm) in ultrasonic sensors?
options: Transducer mechanical ringing after excitation prevents sensing returning echoes immediately
Acoustic waves take 1 second to leave the transducer
Air ionization near the transmitter blocks reception
The receiver is turned off permanently below 5 cm
questions.answer: Transducer mechanical ringing after excitation prevents sensing returning echoes immediately
questions.correct_option: Transducer mechanical ringing after excitation prevents sensing returning echoes immediately
questions.explanation: After transmitting an 8-cycle 40 kHz burst, the piezoelectric crystal continues ringing (decaying resonance). Any echo returning during this time is masked.

questions.question: What triggering electrical pulse width is required by an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor on its Trig pin to initiate a ping?
options: At least 10 µs high-level TTL pulse
A single clock cycle at 16 MHz
questions.answer: At least 10 µs high-level TTL pulse
questions.correct_option: At least 10 µs high-level TTL pulse
questions.explanation: The HC-SR04 specification requires a 10 µs TTL high trigger pulse, which commands the internal ASIC to emit an 8-cycle 40 kHz ultrasound burst.

questions.question: How many ultrasonic wave cycles are typically emitted in a single transmission burst by standard 40 kHz ranging sensors?
questions.answer: 8 cycles
questions.correct_option: 8 cycles
questions.explanation: An 8-cycle burst (lasting 8 / 40,000 = 200 µs) provides sufficient energy to detect reliable echoes while keeping transmission pulse duration short.

questions.question: If the echo pin of an ultrasonic sensor remains HIGH for 1.176 milliseconds, what is the measured one-way distance to the target in air (v = 340 m/s)?
What happens when an ultrasonic beam strikes a smooth, flat surface at a large oblique angle of incidence (> 45°)?
options: Specular reflection deflects the acoustic energy away, resulting in no detectable echo at the receiver
The sound wave is completely absorbed and turned into heat
The sound wave reflects directly back to the sensor regardless of angle
The wave frequency shifts to 80 kHz
questions.answer: Specular reflection deflects the acoustic energy away, resulting in no detectable echo at the receiver
questions.correct_option: Specular reflection deflects the acoustic energy away, resulting in no detectable echo at the receiver
questions.explanation: Smooth surfaces act as acoustic mirrors; by the law of reflection (θ_r = θ_i), energy reflects away from the sensor, causing false 'no target' readings.

questions.question: Why do porous materials like acoustic foam, velvet, and fiberglass make poor ultrasonic targets?
options: They have high acoustic absorption and low reflection coefficient due to impedance damping
They reflect sound faster than the speed of light
They cancel the trigger pulse electrically
questions.answer: They have high acoustic absorption and low reflection coefficient due to impedance damping
questions.correct_option: They have high acoustic absorption and low reflection coefficient due to impedance damping
questions.explanation: Porous, fibrous materials trap air and convert acoustic kinetic energy into viscous heat dissipation, drastically attenuating the returning echo.

questions.question: What is acoustic impedance Z mathematically defined as for a medium?
options: Z = ρ * v (density times speed of sound)
questions.answer: Z = ρ * v (density times speed of sound)
questions.correct_option: Z = ρ * v (density times speed of sound)
questions.explanation: Specific acoustic impedance is the product of mass density ρ and acoustic wave propagation speed v (in Rayls or kg/(m²·s)).

questions.question: Why is an acoustic matching layer placed on the front face of a piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer?
options: To bridge the huge acoustic impedance mismatch between PZT (Z ≈ 30 MRayl) and air (Z ≈ 400 Rayl)
To change the frequency of ultrasound
To provide electrical insulation from ground
questions.answer: To bridge the huge acoustic impedance mismatch between PZT (Z ≈ 30 MRayl) and air (Z ≈ 400 Rayl)
questions.correct_option: To bridge the huge acoustic impedance mismatch between PZT (Z ≈ 30 MRayl) and air (Z ≈ 400 Rayl)
questions.explanation: Without a matching layer (ideally Z_layer = √(Z_pzt * Z_air)), over 99.9% of acoustic energy would reflect back at the crystal-air boundary due to impedance mismatch.

questions.question: What type of acoustic wave propagates through open air from an ultrasonic rangefinder?
questions.answer: Longitudinal compression-rarefaction wave
questions.correct_option: Longitudinal compression-rarefaction wave
questions.explanation: Fluids (gases and liquids) cannot support static shear stresses; hence, acoustic waves in air propagate purely as longitudinal pressure fluctuations.

questions.question: How does relative humidity affect the attenuation of 40 kHz ultrasound in air at room temperature?
options: Molecular relaxation of oxygen/nitrogen causes frequency-dependent absorption that peaks at intermediate humidity levels (~20%-30%)
Higher humidity eliminates all sound attenuation
Sound travels twice as fast in 100% humidity
questions.answer: Molecular relaxation of oxygen/nitrogen causes frequency-dependent absorption that peaks at intermediate humidity levels (~20%-30%)
questions.correct_option: Molecular relaxation of oxygen/nitrogen causes frequency-dependent absorption that peaks at intermediate humidity levels (~20%-30%)
questions.explanation: Water vapor catalysts accelerate vibrational relaxation of oxygen and nitrogen molecules, producing a distinct absorption peak around 20%-30% RH at 40 kHz.

questions.question: What is the typical half-power beam angle (beam divergence) of a standard commercial 40 kHz transducer horn?
questions.answer: Approximately 15° to 30°
questions.correct_option: Approximately 15° to 30°
questions.explanation: Because the transducer diameter (~16 mm) is only about twice the acoustic wavelength (8.5 mm), diffraction creates a cone angle of roughly 15° to 30°.

questions.question: What causes 'crosstalk' in a dual-transducer ultrasonic module (separate transmitter and receiver)?
options: Direct acoustic or structural vibration transmission from transmitter to receiver before reaching the target
Refraction by the earth's magnetic field
questions.answer: Direct acoustic or structural vibration transmission from transmitter to receiver before reaching the target
questions.correct_option: Direct acoustic or structural vibration transmission from transmitter to receiver before reaching the target
questions.explanation: Crosstalk occurs when ultrasonic vibrations leak sideways through the PCB, casing, or direct air path from transmitter to receiver without target reflection.

questions.question: In ultrasonic rangefinding, what is the effect of environmental air turbulence or thermal convection currents (e.g. above a heater)?
options: Causes fluctuations in sound velocity along the path, leading to jitter and noise in distance measurements
Increases the speed of sound to supersonic velocities
Changes the resonant frequency of the piezoelectric crystal
questions.answer: Causes fluctuations in sound velocity along the path, leading to jitter and noise in distance measurements
questions.correct_option: Causes fluctuations in sound velocity along the path, leading to jitter and noise in distance measurements
questions.explanation: Thermal gradients produce localized pockets of varying density and sound speed, refracting the beam and causing acoustic arrival-time jitter.

questions.question: What is the primary disadvantage of using ultrasonic distance meters compared to optical LiDAR sensors?
options: Much slower update rate due to speed of sound (343 m/s vs 3x10⁸ m/s) and wider beam spread
Inability to detect clear glass windows
questions.answer: Much slower update rate due to speed of sound (343 m/s vs 3x10⁸ m/s) and wider beam spread
questions.correct_option: Much slower update rate due to speed of sound (343 m/s vs 3x10⁸ m/s) and wider beam spread
questions.explanation: Sound travels ~1 million times slower than light, limiting sampling rate at long distances (e.g. measuring 4 m takes ~23 ms round-trip). Wide divergence also gives lower spatial resolution.

questions.question: What unique advantage do ultrasonic distance sensors possess over optical time-of-flight sensors?
options: Ultrasonic sensors reliably detect transparent targets like glass and clear acrylic sheets
Ultrasonic waves travel at the speed of light
Ultrasonic sensors work inside a complete vacuum
Ultrasonic sensors have nanometer spatial resolution
questions.answer: Ultrasonic sensors reliably detect transparent targets like glass and clear acrylic sheets
questions.correct_option: Ultrasonic sensors reliably detect transparent targets like glass and clear acrylic sheets
questions.explanation: Transparent materials that let optical light pass through act as solid acoustic boundaries that reflect acoustic pressure waves cleanly.

questions.question: Can an ultrasonic distance meter operate in a vacuum (such as in outer space)?
options: No, acoustic waves require a physical material medium (mass and elasticity) to propagate
Yes, ultrasonic waves are a type of electromagnetic radiation
Yes, but only if the temperature is above 0°C
Yes, because piezoelectric crystals generate their own atmosphere
questions.answer: No, acoustic waves require a physical material medium (mass and elasticity) to propagate
questions.correct_option: No, acoustic waves require a physical material medium (mass and elasticity) to propagate
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical pressure wave consisting of particle collisions; in a vacuum without matter, acoustic propagation is physically impossible.

questions.question: In an experimental calibration of an ultrasonic sensor, what mathematical relationship describes the plotted graph of True Distance (y) vs Echo Time (x)?
options: A straight line passing through the origin with slope equal to v / 2
questions.answer: A straight line passing through the origin with slope equal to v / 2
questions.correct_option: A straight line passing through the origin with slope equal to v / 2
questions.explanation: Since d = (v/2) * t, the relationship is strictly linear with slope m = v/2 and y-intercept near zero (offset by transducer front-face positioning).

questions.question: If linear regression of calibration data yields d = 0.1715 * t (where d is in meters and t in milliseconds), what is the calculated speed of sound?
questions.explanation: Slope = v / 2 = 0.1715 m/ms = 171.5 m/s. Therefore v = 2 * 171.5 m/s = 343.0 m/s.

questions.question: What is the maximum practical range of a standard 40 kHz airborne sensor (e.g. HC-SR04)?
questions.answer: Approximately 4 to 5 meters
questions.correct_option: Approximately 4 to 5 meters
questions.explanation: At 40 kHz, atmospheric absorption (~1.2 dB/m) combined with spherical inverse-square spreading loss limits echo signal-to-noise ratio beyond 4-5 m.

questions.question: If an obstacle is positioned at 3.43 meters distance, what is the total round-trip flight time of the acoustic pulse (at v = 343 m/s)?
questions.answer: 20.0 milliseconds
questions.correct_option: 20.0 milliseconds
questions.explanation: Total round-trip distance = 2 * 3.43 m = 6.86 m. Time t = 6.86 m / 343 m/s = 0.020 s = 20.0 ms.

questions.question: What is the phenomenon called when an echo bounces multiple times between the sensor and target, creating phantom readings at integer multiples of the true distance?
questions.answer: Multipath / multi-bounce reflection
questions.correct_option: Multipath / multi-bounce reflection
questions.explanation: A strong echo reflecting back from the sensor face can travel to the target a second time, producing a false echo at twice the distance if the ping cycle is too fast.

questions.question: What minimum delay between successive measurement pings is recommended to prevent previous echo interference?
questions.answer: Around 50 ms to 60 ms
questions.correct_option: Around 50 ms to 60 ms
questions.explanation: Waiting 50-60 ms between pings gives previous ultrasonic pulses sufficient time to dissipate below the receiver detection threshold.

questions.question: How does the directivity D of an ultrasonic transducer change if its diameter D_transducer is increased at constant frequency?
options: The beam becomes narrower and more directional
The beam spreads wider in all directions
questions.answer: The beam becomes narrower and more directional
questions.correct_option: The beam becomes narrower and more directional
questions.explanation: By diffraction theory, beam divergence half-angle θ ≈ 1.22 λ / D. Increasing aperture diameter D narrows the emission beam.

questions.question: What electronic circuit block inside an ultrasonic receiver amplifies the weak microvolt signal generated by the receiving piezoelectric element?
options: A high-gain bandpass preamplifier and comparator
questions.answer: A high-gain bandpass preamplifier and comparator
questions.correct_option: A high-gain bandpass preamplifier and comparator
questions.explanation: The receiving crystal generates tiny piezoelectric voltages; a multi-stage bandpass amplifier tuned to 40 kHz boosts the signal and a comparator generates a clean digital logic pulse.

questions.question: Why is automatic gain control (Time-Gain Compensation / TGC) often implemented in advanced ultrasonic receivers?
options: To progressively increase amplifier gain over time as echoes arrive from farther, more attenuated targets
To decrease power consumption when idle
To shift the acoustic frequency during flight
To prevent the transmitter from overheating
questions.answer: To progressively increase amplifier gain over time as echoes arrive from farther, more attenuated targets
questions.correct_option: To progressively increase amplifier gain over time as echoes arrive from farther, more attenuated targets
questions.explanation: Echoes from distant targets suffer greater geometric spreading and atmospheric attenuation; Time-Gain Compensation increases gain proportionally with time to equalize sensitivity.

questions.question: What is the acoustic pressure reflection coefficient R at normal incidence between two media of impedances Z1 and Z2?
questions.explanation: The pressure reflection coefficient is R = (Z2 - Z1) / (Z2 + Z1). When Z2 >> Z1 (like air to steel or wall), R ≈ +1, producing near-total reflection.

questions.question: If a moving vehicle approaches an ultrasonic sensor, what physical effect causes the returning frequency to be higher than 40 kHz?
questions.answer: The Doppler Effect
questions.correct_option: The Doppler Effect
questions.explanation: Relative motion between source and receiver shifts the observed wave frequency: f_observed = f_source * (v + v_target) / (v - v_target).

questions.question: What is the wavelength of a 40 kHz acoustic wave in water (where sound speed is v ≈ 1500 m/s)?
questions.explanation: λ = v / f = 1500 m/s / 40,000 Hz = 0.0375 m = 37.5 mm. (Sound travels ~4.4x faster in water than in air).

questions.question: Why does an ultrasonic sensor struggle to measure the distance to a sphere compared to a flat wall?
options: A sphere has only a tiny tangential surface area perpendicular to the beam, scattering most energy away
Spherical objects reflect ultrasound into the 4th dimension
Sound speed slows down near curved objects
questions.answer: A sphere has only a tiny tangential surface area perpendicular to the beam, scattering most energy away
questions.correct_option: A sphere has only a tiny tangential surface area perpendicular to the beam, scattering most energy away
questions.explanation: Curved surfaces act as convex acoustic mirrors that disperse incident acoustic rays outward, leaving only a weak specular echo returning to the sensor.

questions.question: What is the effect of wind blowing parallel to the ultrasonic pulse (towards the target)?
options: The effective speed of sound increases (v_eff = v_sound + v_wind), shortening the round-trip travel time
The frequency of the wave drops to zero
Wind has no effect on sound propagation
questions.answer: The effective speed of sound increases (v_eff = v_sound + v_wind), shortening the round-trip travel time
questions.correct_option: The effective speed of sound increases (v_eff = v_sound + v_wind), shortening the round-trip travel time
questions.explanation: Sound propagates relative to the moving air medium. A tailwind adds to sound velocity on the outward leg, while a headwind subtracts on the return leg.

questions.question: In an experimental calibration curve, what does the y-intercept represent if the model is d = m * t + c?
options: The systematic offset error, including acoustic zero-point distance and internal electronic processing delay
The mass of the transducer crystal
questions.answer: The systematic offset error, including acoustic zero-point distance and internal electronic processing delay
questions.correct_option: The systematic offset error, including acoustic zero-point distance and internal electronic processing delay
questions.explanation: The y-intercept c accounts for the physical distance from the circuit zero to the transducer front face, plus fixed hardware triggering/detector delays.

questions.question: What digital filtering algorithm is commonly used in software to eliminate outlier readings caused by missed ultrasonic pings?
questions.answer: Median filter
questions.correct_option: Median filter
questions.explanation: A median filter over a window of 5-7 readings effectively rejects isolated dropouts (such as 0 cm or 400 cm false spikes) without lagging smooth distance changes.

questions.question: What happens to the acoustic power of an ultrasonic wave as it propagates in free space away from a point-like source?
options: Intensity decreases inversely with the square of distance (1/r²) plus exponential atmospheric absorption
Intensity increases due to acoustic resonance
questions.answer: Intensity decreases inversely with the square of distance (1/r²) plus exponential atmospheric absorption
questions.correct_option: Intensity decreases inversely with the square of distance (1/r²) plus exponential atmospheric absorption
questions.explanation: Geometric spherical spreading reduces acoustic power density according to the inverse-square law (1/r²), supplemented by absorption loss exp(-2αr).

questions.question: Why is the lead zirconate titanate (PZT) crystal in an ultrasonic transducer poled with a strong electric field during manufacturing?
options: To align internal ferroelectric dipoles so the ceramic exhibits macroscopic piezoelectricity
To make the crystal electrically conductive
To melt the crystal into a disc
questions.answer: To align internal ferroelectric dipoles so the ceramic exhibits macroscopic piezoelectricity
questions.correct_option: To align internal ferroelectric dipoles so the ceramic exhibits macroscopic piezoelectricity
questions.explanation: Unpoled polycrystalline PZT has randomly oriented ferroelectric domains that cancel out; poling under high DC field at elevated temperature aligns dipoles to produce strong piezoelectric response.

questions.question: If an ultrasonic sensor is calibrated at 20°C (v = 343.4 m/s) and then used at 40°C (v = 355.3 m/s) without temperature compensation, what percentage error occurs in distance measurement?
questions.answer: Approximately -3.5% (underestimates distance by ~3.5%)
questions.correct_option: Approximately -3.5% (underestimates distance by ~3.5%)
questions.explanation: At 40°C, the echo returns faster. Because the uncompensated firmware calculates d = v_calibrated * t / 2, the calculated distance is (343.4 / 355.3) = 0.9665 of true distance, underestimating by ~3.46%.
